sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the exact word of a line in verse 22 ('fools ___ knowledge'). Nothing on an earlier card lets them reason out 'hate' over 'share' or 'guard', so it is a guess at wording and not a question about meaning.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line. ... The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The story card says 'so they'll be filled with their own devices', which is the second half of verse 31. The next card asks what 'eat the fruit of their own way' means, and the right answer ('they get what their own choices bring') is nearly the same idea. The setup hands the baker the answer and also makes the wrong answers easy to rule out.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
